robot.name: Kawasaki Kaleido 9
robot.status_notes: Kaleido 9 is currently listed as a prototype. It was publicly unveiled at iREX 2025 in Tokyo and remains in the testing phase, with no commercial sale or deployment found.
intended_use_cases: disaster response and hazardous environment operations

height.notes: Humanoid.guide lists 190 cm for Kaleido 9. Robot Overflow lists approximately 5 ft 11 in (~180 cm) for the broader Kaleido family, creating a conflict; the Kaleido 9-specific value is used here.

weight.notes: Humanoid.guide lists 99 kg. Robot Overflow lists approximately 187 lbs (~85 kg) for the broader Kaleido platform; the Kaleido 9-specific value is used here.

payload.notes: Humanoid.guide states 30 kg payload. Robot Overflow describes a Kaleido 9 variant with an 18 kg payload and an earlier generation with a 60 kg arm payload; these are recorded as conflicts, not used for the primary spec.

runtime.notes: Humanoid.guide lists up to 3 hours per charge. Robot Overflow says battery life has not been published by Kawasaki, creating a conflict.

battery.notes: No battery capacity or chemistry was published in the reviewed sources. Robot Overflow explicitly states battery life is not specified.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: No total degrees of freedom for Kaleido 9 was found. Robot Overflow mentions 32 degrees of freedom for the broader Kaleido platform, but this is not clearly tied to Kaleido 9 and is excluded.

walking_speed.notes: Humanoid.guide lists speeds of up to 5 kilometres per hour. Robot Overflow says maximum speed is not specified by Kawasaki, creating a conflict.

hands.description: No detailed hand specifications were found. A disaster rescue demonstration description mentions 'shiny fingers' and gently picking up a toy cat, but hand DoF or tactile capabilities are not disclosed.

sensors.notes: Humanoid.guide states enhanced stereo cameras and LiDAR support three-dimensional mapping.

compute.description: No onboard compute was specified in the reviewed sources. The robot supports Ethernet and WiFi for operational connections.

actuators.description: Fully electric platform with a magnesium alloy skeleton and 3D printed resin exterior panels. Reinforced waist and leg joints are mentioned for balance recovery.

availability.notes: Research and development prototype. Robot Overflow states the robot is not for sale and is an internal R&D platform available free to partner institutions through the YouComeLab programme.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Humanoid.guide rates Manipulation 1 out of 5 and confirms sorting goods as an early applied handling capability. A disaster rescue demonstration description says the robot gently picked up a toy cat and handed it to an MC.
caveats: Very low third-party manipulation score.
Only one brief demonstration description found; no success rates or controlled benchmarks.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Current autonomy is not demonstrated in the reviewed text. Humanoid.guide lists VR headset teleoperation as an operational connection. Ground News reports Kawasaki plans to use Noetra's physical AI to make Kaleido fully autonomous, targeting industrial deployment as early as 2030.
caveats: Existing demos do not clearly state autonomous operation; teleoperation status is not always disclosed.
2030 autonomy is a future media-reported plan, not a current capability.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Humanoid.guide lists speeds up to 5 km/h, confirmed walking stairs, and reinforced waist and leg joints for improved balance recovery.
caveats: No fall rate, disturbance recovery data, or independently verified walking demo found in text sources.
Video titles may show mobility but no transcripts are available for verification.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Humanoid.guide states enhanced stereo cameras and LiDAR support three-dimensional mapping.
caveats: No perception benchmarks or scene-understanding results were found.

human_interaction.summary: Kawasaki's official iREX concept mentions AI, autonomous mobility, voice interaction, and remote operation. A Kawasaki employee article describes a future where Kaleido can engage in conversation while doing heavy labor in an elderly care facility.
caveats: Voice interaction is part of a booth concept and not specifically demonstrated for Kaleido 9 in the reviewed sources.
The employee article is a vision statement and not current product capability.

endurance_reliability.summary: Humanoid.guide lists up to 3 hours per charge. No hardware failure rates, continuous operation data, or reliability benchmarks were found.
caveats: Runtime is a directory figure, not independently verified.
No uptime or intervention logs are available.

human_environment_fit.summary: Kaleido 9 is 190 cm tall and 99 kg, with a magnesium alloy skeleton and reinforced waist and leg joints. Disaster response and demanding industrial environments are the intended use cases.
caveats: No full-robot safety certification was found.
At 99 kg, human-proximity safety is not independently established.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: No commercial deployment or named customer was found. Robot Overflow states there are no known industrial or commercial deployments and the robot is research-only.
caveats: Prototype status with no public deployment metrics.

accessibility_value.summary: Robot Overflow states the robot is not for sale and is available free to partner institutions through Kawasaki's YouComeLab programme. No price or public purchase path exists.
caveats: Access is limited to approved university or research partners and is not a public offer.

evidence_items.title: Kaleido 9 core specifications
evidence_items.claim: Kaleido 9 is a 190 cm, 99 kg fully electric humanoid with a stated 30 kg payload, up to 5 km/h speed, and up to 3 hours runtime per charge.
evidence_items.notes: Directory spec listing; not independently measured. Conflicts with Robot Overflow are recorded separately.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Kaleido 9 is a 190 centimetre humanoid robot from Kawasaki Robotics, created for disaster response and demanding industrial environments. The fully electric platform weighs 99 kilograms, has a stated payload strength of 30 kilograms, reaches speeds of up to 5 kilometres per hour, and operates for up to three hours per charge.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Humanoid.guide and Robot Overflow conflict on payload (30 kg vs 18 kg), speed (5 km/h vs not published), runtime (3 h vs not published), height/weight, and DoF. No official Kawasaki specification page was found in the reviewed sources.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Specs should be treated as uncertain; use directory figures with low confidence.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Several YouTube sources are titles only. They cannot be used to verify mobility, manipulation, or autonomy claims.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: No current fully autonomous operation was found; Humanoid.guide lists VR headset teleoperation as a primary input. Ground News reports a future plan for full autonomy by 2030 using Noetra physical AI.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Total DoF, hand DoF, battery capacity, onboard compute, price, and independent benchmarks are absent.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Kaleido 9 is a Kawasaki heavy-lift-capable bipedal prototype focused on disaster response and industrial use, but current public evidence is thin and mostly directory-based. It is not for sale and has no commercial deployment or verified autonomous operation.
strongest_positive_evidence: Official Kawasaki event page confirms first public unveiling at iREX 2025.
Humanoid.guide lists core specs: 190 cm, 99 kg, 30 kg payload, up to 5 km/h, 3 hours runtime.
Disaster rescue demonstration description includes gentle toy cat pick-up, suggesting basic manipulation.
Kawasaki has a long-term vision for humanoid collaboration and a future physical AI autonomy plan.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No current autonomous demo or disclosure of teleoperation status in most sources.
No named customer, deployment, or field test.
No price, DoF, battery capacity, or compute specs.
Video titles cannot be used to verify capabilities.
conflicting_claims: Payload: 30 kg (Humanoid.guide) vs 18 kg Kaleido 9 variant (Robot Overflow).
Speed: up to 5 km/h (Humanoid.guide) vs not published (Robot Overflow).
Runtime: up to 3 hours (Humanoid.guide) vs not published (Robot Overflow).
Height/weight: 190 cm / 99 kg (Humanoid.guide) vs ~5'11" / 187 lbs (Robot Overflow for broader Kaleido).
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit current full autonomy or adaptation from video titles alone.
Do not credit 32 DoF or 60 kg arm payload to Kaleido 9; these refer to earlier/broader platform data.
Do not describe Kaleido 9 as commercially deployed or field-tested.
Do not treat the disaster rescue toy cat demo as verified without the original article or video.

currentness.currentness_notes: Kaleido 9 is the latest publicly shown Kaleido generation as of the reviewed sources; no newer Kawasaki humanoid generation was found.

excluded_claims.reason: Robot Overflow mentions 32 DoF for the broader Kaleido platform, not clearly for Kaleido 9; no official DoF found.
These figures belong to earlier Kaleido generations or original claims, not Kaleido 9. Robot Overflow notes the Kaleido 9 payload as 18 kg, conflicting with Humanoid.guide's 30 kg.
No current autonomy evidence was found; only a future plan for 2030 full autonomy via Noetra physical AI.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Kawasaki Kaleido 9 is a 190 cm, 99 kg bipedal industrial humanoid prototype, publicly unveiled at iREX 2025 and still in the testing phase. Humanoid.guide lists a stated 30 kg payload, up to 5 km/h speed, and up to 3 hours runtime, but Robot Overflow conflicts on several specs and says Kawasaki has not published official battery or speed figures. A textual disaster rescue description says it gently picked up a toy cat, and Humanoid.guide confirms walking stairs and sorting goods as capabilities, with low manipulation and navigation scores. Current autonomy is not demonstrated; VR headset teleoperation is listed, and Ground News reports a 2030 plan for full autonomy using Noetra physical AI. The robot is not for sale and has no commercial deployment or named customer.
strongest_evidence: Official Kawasaki iREX 2025 event page confirms first public unveiling.
Disaster rescue demonstration description shows basic gentle pick-up.
Humanoid.guide confirms walking stairs and sorting goods.
Kawasaki employee article documents long-term disaster and elderly care vision.
weakest_evidence: No current autonomous operation or clear teleoperation disclosure.
No independent battery/speed verification; directory conflicts.
No commercial deployment, field test, or customer.
Video sources lack transcripts and cannot be used for verification.
known_do_not_credit: 32 DoF or 60 kg arm payload for Kaleido 9.
Commercial deployment or field rescue use.
Capabilities from video titles without transcripts.
